notes:
Undated typescript contents continuation numbered ‘- 541 -’; archive 85 is recorded in a comment. It has no independent title, signature or total page count. The page contains 25 numbered entries, 3.8–3.10, 4.1–4.6, 5.1–5.5 and 6.1–6.11, plus headings for immersions and reduced schemes, separated morphisms and valuative criteria, and relative finiteness conditions. Entries 3.10 and 6.8 have no dotted leader. No authorial question or explicit doubt is written.

Six overtyped positions remain visible. The two Jacobson initials and the j under n in ‘Détermination’ are confirmed; a/e beneath d and s/b beneath f remain unresolved. The low contour at the corrected i in ‘schématique’ supports adding j to l/t as an alternative, but does not establish its relation to the older letter; its observed shape is retained within the same correction cluster. All five explicit C doubts remain, two with more faithful graphic treatment or revised alternatives. The low mark beside the §4 period and the detached pair above 6.3 have uncertain functions. The pale channel cutting a leader dot is treated as surface disruption, not manuscript writing. H has description only; there are no H collation rows and no mathematical proof or computation is claimed.
math_reading_decisions: C-context 5.3: the live de is independently confirmed; d has a high ascender and low bowl, while the overprinted a/e remains uncertain and is separately reported.
C-context 5.5: live valuatifs is independently confirmed; f has its hooked upper head, tall stem and transverse stroke, while the older s/b remains uncertain and is separately reported.

C-context 6.4: the first ordinary typed J has a top cap and low left hook over a smaller d bowl/right ascender; the second ordinary typed J covers a dotted lower-case j with a surviving low descender. Both C underprints d and j are confirmed in half b without reopening the loci.
C-context 6.6: the live n has two uprights joined by an arch; the older dot and downward hook identify j beneath it in Détermination. C is confirmed from half b.

C-context 6.10: the live word schématique and replacement i are confirmed; the older l/t remains unresolved and the low surviving foot also permits j. The alternatives are recorded in decision A086-07.
The capital S in 5.1 has one ordinary curved typed outline, with no independent doubled stroke; $S$ is retained. There are no formulas, mathematical displays, arrows or indices on this contents page.

Every section sign has the opposed curved loops, and the numbered labels and decimal points were checked independently. The leader series are present except after 3.10 and 6.8; those two entries end in text without leaders.
Typed pagination reads 541 with a dash on either side, and the separate handwritten archive numeral reads 85.

Main retained comma/period after schéma from its degraded angular impression; the following capital does not supply a punctuation decision. The low contour below the corrected i was compared as part of the same uncertain letter cluster, with j added as a possibility rather than asserted as its identity.
